sanskrit_verse:
अशक्तालसरोगार्तबालभीतप्रवासिनाम् ।
शासनारूढं अन्येन भुक्तं भुक्त्या न हीयते ॥
transliteration: aśaktālasarogārtabālabhītapravāsinām / śāsanārūḍham anyena bhuktaṃ bhuktyā na hīyate
sph_interpretive_translation: That which is consumed by another on behalf of the incapacitated, diseased, lazy, distressed child, frightened or displaced individual, under lawful authority, is not to be reclaimed through litigation or contest.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derived from capacity deficit recognition
Causation through representation and lawful delegation
Restoration logic rooted in existential necessity
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent A acts under lawful authority FOR incapacitated party B, THEN consumption of resources by A for B's sustenance SHALL NOT be subject to restitution.
IF party B is incapable due to illness, fear, displacement, youth or exhaustion, THEN any resource utilization by authorized representative C IS deemed non-contestable.
IF a transaction occurs under recognized dharma-adhikara, THEN no civil or legal reversal SHALL be executed.
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, when incapacity is established—whether physical, psychological, circumstantial or developmental—the court MUST recognize lawful representation as sufficient cause to bar restitution claims. The threshold of responsibility lies in verifying the legitimacy of the representative's authority, not in punitive inquiry into usage.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that action taken under verified incapacity is causally complete without requiring punitive oversight. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential understanding: first incapacity, then representation, then lawful consumption. Responsibility aligns with capacity, not ownership. This upholds Dharma without invoking suffering-based deterrents.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Verification of claimed incapacity through pramāṇa-based inquiry
Authorization validation through community or spiritual witness
Completion process ensuring needs are fully met before adjudication
Reintegration support for the represented party post-resolution
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. Justice flows from consciousness, not coercion. This law restores integrity, not inflicts penalty. Reality is non-punitive; consciousness is the ultimate judge.
